"How to Finance Conflict Worldwide" -- The Journal of Psychoactive Drugs

March 14, 1998

See

HOW THE NARCS CREATED CRACKby Richard C. Cowan
and
How the Establishment Media Suppresses Coverage of CIA's Hard Drug Trafficking
--Fairness & Accuracy In Reporting

March 14, 1998

See

From Journal of Psychoactive Drugs

Vol. 20 (4), Oct-Dec 1988 p.464

Author—Giancarlo Arnao

...."one can tentatively construct a scenario for the evolution of the illicit drug trade. This trend [toward more pharmacologically concentrated synthetic substances] has already been realized in some producing countries, where people have traditionally used coca leaves or crude opium for centuries. In these countries, the prohibitionist drug policy imposed by the United Nations has brought about the disappearance of the natural products and the widespread use of their chemically refined derivatives (e.g., cocaine, morphine, heroin).

This has occurred in Pakistan, for example, where heroin addiction was unknown until 1979, when opium use was banned by the Zia government. Now heroin affects at least 300,000 and possibly one million people (Whitaker 1987: 322).** The same phenomenon was reported in Hong Kong after the opium ban in 1945 (Whitaker 1987: 68), in Laos after the opium ban in 1971 (Whitaker 1987: 66) and in Thailand (International Narcotics control Board 1987). Whitaker, B. 1987. "The Global Connection." London: Jonathan Cape.

** Current (1998) figures indicate 1 ½ million heroin users in Pakistan!

*** (So opium was banned in Pakistan in 1979....and heroin became a cash crop shortly thereafter to help finance the Afghan Conflict. Coincidence? There is something very perverse about the International Narcotics Control Board—EES)
